Definition: to twine, i.e. (literally) to struggle or (figuratively) be (morally) tortuous
BiblicalUsage: Pathal means to twine, to wrestle, to be crooked or tortuous. Rachel says in Genesis 30:8, with great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed, and names her son Naphtali. David says in 2 Samuel 22:27 that with the froward God will show Himself unsavoury, and the same words stand in Psalm 18:26.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that wrestling runs through this word, from Rachel wrestling her sister to God wrestling the crooked, and the name Naphtali carries the struggle in it.
